names.name: Long John
names.said: Midwestern by default. In California the same thing is a bar.

text.what: A bar-shaped raised donut, glazed all over or iced on top, sometimes filled with custard or cream.
text.story: Names for it are regional in a way few American foods still are. Long John dominates the Midwest, Canada and Texas. The Mid-Atlantic and central Canada market it as an éclair; the pastries look alike but an éclair is steam-puffed choux with fondant, and a Long John is yeast. The West Coast says bar. Parts of the Midwest say finger doughnut, or cream stick when it is filled.
text.how: Cut from sheeted raised dough into rectangles, proofed, fried, then glazed or iced. Filling goes in from the end with a nozzle.
text.today: A filled Long John is one of the few donuts a shop will cut open for you to prove what is inside.
